passage:
A coastal museum displayed a bell from an old ship. Visitors could not ring it, but they could listen to a recording of its sound.
The guide explained that the bell had helped sailors mark time and signal danger. During fog, sound could matter more than sight.
A student touched the glass case and imagined the bell ringing over dark water.
The bell was silent now, but its purpose was clear. It had once helped people survive when they could not see far ahead.
The museum visit taught the student that old objects are not just decorations. They are answers to problems people once faced.
